row.Finding description: Reducing SDS-PAGE of preparations containing ApoE3 or ApoE4 showed approximately 70-kDa bands assigned to ApoE dimers, including ApoE-only aggregate controls, without reporting whether dimer abundance differed between isoforms.
row.Finding quote: We observed also some higher molecular weight bands of ~70 kDa in SDS-PAGE lanes, as shown in Figure 4A, corresponding to S100A9 aggregated with ApoE isoforms. These bands correspond to the dimer of ApoE as they appeared in the lanes, which contain only ApoE aggregates (Figure 4A).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (relative ApoE dimer abundance unresolved; ApoE dimers reported in the isoform experiment)
row.Experimental system: Cell-free recombinant human ApoE3 and ApoE4 preparations, with lipid-free and DOPC/cholesterol-lipidated samples included. Fig 4A examines samples after 70 h at 42 °C in PBS using reducing SDS-PAGE and Coomassie staining; co-incubation samples contained 50 μM S100A9 and 2 μM ApoE. ApoE-only controls were also loaded. The text does not resolve the dimer signal by every lipidation/isoform lane.

row.Finding quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D).

row.Finding description: Astrocytes accumulated more ApoE4 than ApoE3. The reported overlap coefficients for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE were 0.497 ± 0.090 for E4 and 0.410 ± 0.049 for E3. Differential receptor retention remains unresolved.
row.Finding quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4) (Figure 2I).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more internalized ApoE and more ApoE-containing lysosomal compartments)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes from ThermoFisher A18945; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day; ApoE/LDLR/LAMP1 imaging, internalized ApoE quantification and Mander’s overlap analysis.

row.Finding quote: Super-resolution imaging on APOE KO iAstrocytes confirmed internalized lipApoE completely colocalized with endogenous LDLR (Mander’s coefficient for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LDLR = 1 for all 3 isoforms), largely inside LAMP1 compartments (Figure 2H) (Mander’s coefficients for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LAMP1 = 0.823 ± 0.061 for ApoE2; 0.903 ± 0.024 for ApoE3; 0.900 ± 0.008 for ApoE4).

row.Finding description: Live imaging of transferrin transport in isogenic human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells showed frequent sorting-tubule formation and vesicle fission in APOE3 cells but reduced sorting-tubule formation in APOE4 cells.
row.Finding quote: In agreement with previous data on mouse brain endothelial cells (Villaseñor et al., 2017), we observed frequent events of sorting tubule biogenesis and vesicle fission in ApoE3 iCE-BECs (Figure 5G; Videos S1 and S2). In contrast, the number of sorting tubules was substantially reduced in ApoE4 iCE-BECs (Figure 5H).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (reduced transferrin-positive sorting-tubule formation in human iCE-BECs)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells (iCE-BECs), isogenic pair 1: homozygous APOE3 Bioni037-A (16423), originating from healthy-donor fibroblasts, versus its gene-edited homozygous APOE4 derivative Bioni037-A4 (I40-53); experiments performed on differentiation day 14 by default; incubated with 25 μg/mL Tf-Alexafluor488 for 3 h before live fluorescence imaging at 100×, acquiring 2 frames/s for 1 min.
row.Data location: Fig 5G (representative events) and Fig 5H (genotype comparison of tubule formation)

row.Finding description: Live imaging of isogenic pair 1 human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells showed fewer transferrin-positive endosomal sorting tubules forming in APOE4 than APOE3 cells across three independent differentiations with 20 videos per experiment, providing a sorting surrogate without establishing ARF6 involvement.
row.Finding quote: In contrast, the number of sorting tubules was substantially reduced in ApoE4 iCE-BECs (Figure 5H).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (reduced transferrin-positive endosomal sorting tubule formation in human iCE-BECs)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived brain endothelial cells (iCE-BECs), isogenic pair 1: homozygous APOE3 Bioni037-A (16423), derived from a healthy individual's fibroblasts, versus homozygous APOE4 Bioni037-A4 (I40-53), generated by editing the parental APOE allele; donor age not stated. Experiments used day 14 cells under the default methods schedule. Cells were incubated with 25 μg/mL transferrin-Alexafluor488 for 3 h and imaged live for 1 min at 100×; two independent blinded raters manually counted sorting tubules, reported as formation events per 1,000 μm2 per minute.

row.Finding description: Across three LysoIP replicates, human-APOE4-expressing murine Neuro-2a cells showed greater lysosomal APOE abundance than human-APOE3-expressing cells, providing an accumulation surrogate without measuring apoE aggregation.
row.Finding quote: Through this approach, we found that HsAPOE4-expressing lysosomes accumulated APOE itself, AD-associated secretase proteins (PSEN2, CD63, TSPAN3), trafficking receptors (AP1S1, AP1G1, BET1L, LAMTOR1, LAMTOR2, TMED5), and lipid/glycan-regulators (ACSL4, ACBD3, GALNT2, MAN2B1, NEU1, PIP4P1, SACM1L, PIP4P1/TMEM55B, UXS1) (Figure 3B,C, Figure S3C).
row.Experimental system: Male murine Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells carrying full-length human APOE3 or APOE4 genomic transgenes; endogenous mouse Apoe retained; passages 5–10; basal untreated condition; TMEM192-3xHA LysoIP followed by quantitative DIA mass spectrometry with lysosomal-tag normalization.
